text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Internal soap production dropped by 50 percent in the past six years. Import soared due to low tax levels for soap.
- The State Ownership Fund (FPS) will liquidate loss-making companies and financially support the profit-making ones, FPS president Sorin Dimitriu said in interview.
ADEVARUL
- Former president of private Bankcoop SA bank Alexandru Dinulescu was arrested on suspicions of bribe taking.
- The government drafts a set of tax relaxation measures which could be enforced in the fourth quarter, senator Varujan Vosganian, chairman of the Senate finance commission said.
- The National Bank abandoned computing the reference rate for the local leu currency as part of steps to liberalise the foreign exchange market.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Employers' Association asked the government to allow full tax exemptions for reinvesting. Current legislation provides exemptions for 50 percent of the reinvested profit.
- Electricity price set at 365 lei per kilowatt was computed at an exchange rate of 7,300 lei to the dollar.
- Major state-owned Bancorex bank rose its interest rate for one-month deposits to 85 percent.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Inflation rose to 13.7 percent in January 1997 from December 1996 and was 76.3 percent year-on-year.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Newspaper prints interview with French President Jacques Chirac, ahead of his Romania visit. "Romania must be on the first NATO integration wave," Chirac said.

- A chance for Romania to openly defend its case regarding admission to NATO -- paper says of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's proposal that each of the candidates to NATO membership be invited to Brussels to plead own cause.
- Romanians who seek asylum in France now pretend that they are supporters of ex-President Ion Iliescu, believing that they may boost their chances to be allowed to stay, paper says.
- Paper quotes Radu Vasile, spokesman for the ruling National Peasant Party, as saying that so far the centrist coalition government has made many blunders.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Paper compiles media reports on the death of China's veteran leader Deng Xiaoping.
- Full-page report on inmates' protests at the Jilava jail.
- During its Friday meeting, the government will discuss decree on restoring former King Michael's Romanian citizenship, which was stripped from him by former Communists 49 years ago.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- There will be 10 percent layoffs among public administration officials, government's secretary-general Remus Opris said during meeting with local county prefects.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
